questions.question_text:
The diagram shows a pyramid with a rectangular base of sides $9\text{ cm}$ and $7\text{ cm}$.
The apex-to-corner edge is $17\text{ cm}$.
Work out the vertical height of the pyramid.

options.why: Uses the full base diagonal instead of the distance from the centre to a corner.
Uses an approximate or incomplete subtraction of squared lengths.
Gives a height greater than the sloping edge, which is geometrically impossible.

questions.solution_text: The distance from the centre of the rectangular base to corner C is half the base diagonal: $r=\frac12\sqrt{9^2+7^2}=\frac{\sqrt{130}}2$. Hence $h^2+r^2=17^2$, so $h=\sqrt{289-130/4}=\sqrt{256.5}\approx16.0\text{ cm}$.
